methodology.scope: Slide-level active Choice content; master/layout sample text, notes and raster labels excluded.
methodology.character_weight: Unicode code points inside text runs, including spaces; paragraph/line-break markers excluded.
methodology.object_weight: Each nonempty text-bearing shape has one vote based on its character-dominant font or size. Objects-containing distributions overlap.
methodology.font: Latin typeface declaration, resolving theme aliases. Actual font substitution at render time requires PowerPoint/font inspection.
methodology.color: OOXML theme mapping plus sRGB and HSL luminance transforms; resolved 8-bit hex may differ by one unit from Office rounding.
methodology.geometry: Axis-aligned bounds clipped to canvas. Coverage means object-box coverage, not glyph pixels or aesthetic blank space.
methodology.inheritance: Run > paragraph default > local list style > placeholder hierarchy > master text style > presentation default. Shape fontRef supplies color ahead of generic master otherStyle.
methodology.default_spacing: Absent inherited spacing recorded as single line, zero before/after per OOXML default. Verify renderer with COM if exact display needed.
methodology.math: Modern Choice OMML included separately; Fallback raster excluded. Declared 28 pt does not equal rendered subscript size.
methodology.roles: Reference-specific heuristic: Times New Roman = body; Elephant >=70pt = cover/closing display; Elephant <=20pt = metadata; other Elephant = slide title; all-math shape = formula. Inspect semantic classification before applying to another deck.
limitations: No image attribution or painting medium determined from XML.
No assumptions that every image is a paper screenshot.
Paragraph default spacing and shape fontRef inheritance need renderer corroboration.
OOXML text margins use defaults when absent.

references.text:
Delta-radiomics measures changes in quantitative imaging features between scans taken at different time points. 

It can help assess treatment response or disease progression earlier by detecting changes beyond tumor size alone.

1. Serial image acquisition
Collect baseline and follow-up scans at defined treatment times.
2. Image preprocessing
Improve comparability through appropriate registration, resampling, and intensity normalization.
3. ROI segmentation
Delineate the tumor region at each time point.
4. Radiomic feature extraction
Extract corresponding shape, intensity, and texture features using consistent settings.

5. Delta feature calculation
Calculate the change in each corresponding feature.

6. Feature selection
Select stable and informative features, and remove redundant features using training data.
7. Model development
Train a prediction model for treatment response, survival, or recurrence.

8. Model evaluation
Evaluate model performance using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, then validate it on independent data.
Guo et al. used early MRI changes to predict pathological complete response (pCR) at surgery after treatment.

Delta outperformed baseline (p = 0.047); while the difference from cycle 1 was not significant (p = 0.500).

Single-center evidence; external validation is needed.

Changes in scan settings or tumor boundaries can look like treatment effects.
Guo’s results are encouraging, but validation in 42 patients from one hospital leaves a question: how well would the model work elsewhere?

I would first test whether the same feature changes remain useful across hospitals.
For me, the key question is whether an early prediction helps doctors make a better treatment decision.
